summary: The unmatched behavior is the ghoul’s monster-to-hero AD_PLYS claw, whose source owner is uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys(). The current evaluation matches 28/37 screens, 2275/2371 RNG calls, and 28/37 cursors, then stops at step 28 when JS uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() dispatches AD_PLYS to its unported refusal. C reaches mhitu.c:hitmu() and uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys(), prints the attack message, and consumes rn2(3)=2; that value fails the paralysis-chance test, so this recording proves the helper/message path is reached but does not show the hero becoming paralyzed. The actionable scope is a whole-function port of uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys() and replacing the AD_PLYS dispatcher refusal while preserving its three attacker/defender branches and all existing dispatch callers. Its consumed mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() boolean already has a JS implementation. The successful-paralysis path also calls void uhitm.c:dynamic_multi_reason(), for which JS has no matching helper; retain that named void gap if it is not included. No replay was needed because the admitted C recording, saved evaluation and source show the reached branch and refusal.

source.branch: A hostile ghoul summoned with the Wizard command gets a movement opportunity while the player waits, closes to an attack, and lands its first AT_CLAW attack (AD_PLYS, 1d2). monmove.c:dochug() sends it through the standard monster-to-hero attack path; mhitu.c:hitmu() passes the AD_PLYS attack to uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping(), which selects mhitm_ad_plys(). In the saved C step 28, rn2(3)=2 fails the paralysis chance, but the helper still emits the hit message and consumes that chance roll.
callers: C runtime route: monmove.c:dochug() standard attack gate (965-972) -> mhitu.c:mattacku() melee hit path (812) -> mhitu.c:hitmu() (1143 onward), which calls uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() at 1191 -> uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys() from the AD_PLYS dispatcher at 4815. JS route: unported_monster_actions.js:runSimpleMonsterAction() (1566-1587) configures attackHeroWithMattacku() (1482-1485); monmove.js:dochug() invokes it at 2773 -> mhitu.js:mattacku()/hitmu() (1178, 1650-1707) -> uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping() AD_PLYS arm at 4836, which currently throws through the unsupported callback.

The shared uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() dispatcher is also called by mhitm.c:mdamagem() at 1059 and uhitm.c:damageum() at 4854. Preserve those production routes: JS mhitm.js:mdamagem() calls it at 1057, and JS uhitm.js:damageum() calls it at 4886; they supply the hero-to-monster and monster-to-monster branches of the same helper.
dependencies: C uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys() (3431-3476) is void and has three branches selected by whether magr or mdef is gy.youmonst: hero-to-monster, monster-to-hero, and monster-to-monster. All are part of the whole-function scope. In this case the monster-to-hero branch calls hitmsg(magr, mattk), tests gm.multi >= 0, consumes rn2(3), and uses the boolean returned by mhitm_mgc_atk_negated(magr, mdef, TRUE) to gate paralysis. JS hitmsg() already exists in mhitu.js, and JS mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() exists at uhitm.js:776-815.

When a paralysis gate succeeds, the hero branch tests Free_action; otherwise Blind selects the message, rnd(10) supplies the nomul duration, nomul() installs the delay, dynamic_multi_reason() writes the monster-specific multi_reason, and exercise(A_DEX, FALSE) updates dexterity exercise. JS has nomul(), exercise(), and the related monster paralyze_monst() implementation for the other attacker/defender branches. The C rn2(3)=2 in this recording fails the chance condition, so it does not reach mhitm_mgc_atk_negated(), nomul(), or dynamic_multi_reason().

uhitm.c:dynamic_multi_reason() (103-123) is a void state-writing callee with no JS counterpart; `rg -n 'dynamic_multi_reason' js/uhitm.js js/mhitu.js js/mhitm.js` returns no matches. If it remains outside the implementation scope, record and skip it as `note_unported("uhitm.c dynamic_multi_reason")` rather than inventing a return value. No return from mhitm_ad_plys() or mhitm_adtyping() is consumed by their callers.

Immutable C recording challenges/cases/v18/wizard-hostile-ghoul-AD-PLYS-wander-pursuit-c59.session.json: step 26 creates the hostile ghoul, step 27 is a wait without an attack, and step 28 is a wait on which C shows “The ghoul hits! The ghoul hits again!”. On that step C logs `rnd(20)=4 @ mattacku`, `d(1,2)=2 @ hitmu`, and `rn2(3)=2 @ mhitm_ad_plys(uhitm.c:3446)`. Because 2 is nonzero, the C paralysis chance fails; this is evidence of the helper and hit-message path, not a successful paralysis effect.

C source defines the ghoul’s first two attacks as AT_CLAW/AD_PLYS 1d2 then AT_CLAW/AD_PHYS 1d3 in nethack-c/upstream/include/monsters.h:2478-2483. monmove.c:dochug() sends an eligible hostile monster through mattacku() at 965-972; mhitu.c:mattacku() calls hitmu() for its landed melee hit at 812; mhitu.c:hitmu() calls uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() at 1191; uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() dispatches AD_PLYS to mhitm_ad_plys() at 4815.

The source function uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_plys() at 3431-3476 handles uhitm, mhitu and mhitm attacker/defender orientations. In the recorded mhitu orientation it calls hitmsg() before the gm.multi/rn2(3) paralysis gate. The first recorded rn2(3)=2 bypasses the consumed mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() return and the paralysis side effects, explaining why the C screen reports hits but not freezing.

Current JS has the same outer route: unported_monster_actions.js:runSimpleMonsterAction() supplies attackHeroWithMattacku(); monmove.js:dochug() calls that operation at 2773; mhitu.js:mattacku() reaches hitmu() at 1178; hitmu() calls uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping() at 1707. The dispatcher’s AD_PLYS arm at uhitm.js:4836 calls unported("mhitm_ad_plys"); unported_monster_actions.js:214-224 turns that name into the observed UnsupportedSimpleMonsterActionError. This is the missing source function, not an inference from the downstream RNG caller tag.

Other production paths share the dispatcher: C mhitm.c:mdamagem() (1059) and uhitm.c:damageum() (4854); JS mhitm.js:mdamagem() (1057) and uhitm.js:damageum() (4886). The helper port and dispatcher wiring must retain those existing callers.

C mhitm_ad_plys() consumes the boolean result of uhitm.c:mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() in its chance-success branch; JS already implements the helper at uhitm.js:776-815, including the consumed rn2(10) and optional message. C dynamic_multi_reason() at uhitm.c:103-123 has no JS counterpart (confirmed by the cited rg search) and remains a conditional void gap if the successful paralysis branch is not expanded to port it.

Historical counter-evidence from the exact C recording: although the case is specifically selected for AD_PLYS, the first `rn2(3)=2` gate does not establish that paralysis occurred. The saved screen states only that the ghoul hit twice. Keep the source port general across all three C branches; do not describe this case as a successful frozen-status outcome.
